program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s target and relation are broadly clear, but its binding is malformed/duplicated and does not explicitly anchor the comparison to both source and edited images. Repair the typed binding so it identifies the source book and rose, then assesses the same objects’ edited positions against the requested depth relation. Preserve the rubric’s distinction: movement toward the rose alone is not partial unless the book’s placement shows progress toward being behind it; unrelated object changes (here, the book appears split/altered and the rose becomes two flowers) are not requested progress. The traces mostly support absent: the edited book and flowers remain separate, with no visible occlusion/depth ordering. One trace calls the book shifted toward the flowers and labels partial, but gives no concrete positional evidence that this movement advances the behind relation; make the criterion require evidence of relation-directed progress, not proximity alone. Do not force the reference ‘no’: the aggregate is 4 no / 1 partial, and the disagreement warrants clearer evidence-based classification rather than answer bias. All traces are valid, queried, and dependency-free, so this is not a transport/schema failure; high confidence and repeated absent judgments support the current conclusion, while the single partial trace merits criterion calibration.
